criteria.criterion: A store-wide sweep performs exactly one history walk regardless of ticket count — a test counts BOTH the per-sweep builder and the per-ticket/per-event resolvers, so a key-shape mismatch that silently falls back to per-event walks fails the test rather than passing on identical output.
No history walk runs inside the store write lock — a test instruments both and asserts no walk observes the lock held.

SUPERSEDED, recorded not deleted: no prep/commit TOCTOU window exists to guard. The plan proposed hoisting the whole fold out of the lock and re-checking the event set under it. What shipped is narrower — only the HISTORY WALK moved out (`_sweep_position_map`, built once per sweep before any lock); the fold still runs entirely inside `_compact_locked`. That removes the git-log cost from the critical section without splitting it, so there is no window and nothing to re-check.
The authorship ledger is unchanged by the optimisation — a test compares ledgers built with and without the prebuilt map on signed, unsigned and forged-signature events.
The map argument is optional and the fsck rebuild path is unaffected — a test calls `_build_authorship_ledger` without it (as `compact_rebuild.py:160` does) and asserts the same ledger as before.
The compaction commit contains only folded paths — a test asserts a concurrent writer's uncommitted event file is not swept into it.
A sweep stands aside mid-run when a writer takes the lock, leaving remaining tickets unfolded — and the full local gate set plus CI's pytest tiers pass.
Bug 'Sweep walks full git history per ticket under the store lock' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces and expected behavior holds.
